title: U.S. House · Kentucky's 2nd District
area: South-central Kentucky, including Bowling Green, Owensboro and Elizabethtown.

candidates.name: Brett Guthrie
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, Kentucky's 2nd District (since 2009); Chair, House Committee on Energy and Commerce

summary.text: Brett Guthrie is the Republican incumbent for Kentucky's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2008. A West Point graduate and former Army officer, he worked in his family's Bowling Green manufacturing business and served in the Kentucky State Senate before entering Congress. He chairs the House Committee on Energy and Commerce in the 119th Congress.

background.text: Born in 1964 in Florence, Alabama, according to Ballotpedia. His official biography describes his family's Bowling Green, Kentucky, manufacturing business.
Earned a bachelor's degree in economics from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 1987 and a master's degree in Public and Private Management from Yale University in 1997.

Served in the U.S. Army from 1987 to 1990 and the U.S. Army Reserve from 1990 to 2002. His official biography says he was a Field Artillery Officer in the 101st Airborne Division (Air Assault) at Fort Campbell.
After his Army service, joined Trace Die Cast, a Bowling Green manufacturing business started by his father, according to his official biography.
First elected to public office in 1998, he represented the 32nd District in the Kentucky State Senate from 1999 until his election to Congress in 2008.
Elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 2008 and has served Kentucky's 2nd District since 2009.
Chairs the House Committee on Energy and Commerce in the 119th Congress, a panel with jurisdiction over energy, the environment, health care, telecommunications and consumer product safety.
Has served as a Deputy Whip within the House Republican Conference for three terms, according to his official biography.
According to his official biography, he is married to the former Beth Clemmons and they have three children and several grandchildren.

priorities.text: Technology: focused on improving cellular and broadband service in rural areas and "maintaining America's technological competitive edge against the Chinese Communist Party."
Health Care: as Chair of the Energy and Commerce Committee's Health Subcommittee, says he advances policies to lower costs through competition and price transparency.
Fiscal Responsibility: says he wants to get the national debt under control and has consistently supported a balanced budget amendment to the Constitution.

positions.summary: Says climate change is a real threat but opposes the Green New Deal and other rapid, mandated shifts away from fossil fuels, favoring an "all-of-the-above" energy strategy and market-based solutions instead.
positions.quote: I am a member of the Conservative Climate Caucus and think that climate change is a real and serious threat. However, I do not believe that radical solutions proposed in the Democrats’ “Green New Deal” are the solution. The Green New Deal is projected to cost up to $93 trillion over ten years, at an estimated cost of over $60,000 per year per household. I believe that we need innovative and market-based solutions to combat climate change.

positions.summary: Opposes proposed changes to the stepped-up basis and capital gains tax, saying they could force families to sell farms.
positions.quote: I strongly oppose Democrat policies like the methane tax, or proposed changes to the current stepped-up basis and capital gains tax that could force families to sell their farms.

positions.summary: Calls Democratic proposals for government-run health care financially "disastrous," grouping it with other policies he opposes as reckless spending.
positions.quote: The Democrats’ proposed policies such as the Green New Deal, government-run health care, and other reckless spending packages would be disastrous for the financial stability of our country.

record.text: Chairs the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (119th Congress, 2025-2026).
Chaired the Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Health in the 118th Congress (2023-2024) before becoming full committee chair.

candidates.name: Megan Wingfield
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 40.7% of the vote, defeating Hank Linderman, David Hatfield and William Compton.

summary.text: Megan Wingfield, the Democratic nominee, is a mechanic from Bowling Green, Kentucky. Her campaign website describes her as a caregiver and activist who is running on working families, affordable healthcare and a fair shot for every Kentucky family.

background.text: According to her campaign website, she was born and raised in Bowling Green, Kentucky.
Graduated from Southcentral Kentucky Community and Technical College (SKYCTC) with a degree in Automotive Technology and worked as a mechanic.
Her campaign website says she built her career as a mechanic and describes her as a caregiver and activist.

priorities.text: Campaigns on affordable healthcare and support for working families.

positions.summary: Campaigns for affordable healthcare access as a central issue.

summary.text: Thomas Loecken is an independent candidate for Kentucky's 2nd Congressional District. He also appeared on the 2018 ballot in this district as an independent. No campaign website or biographical profile was found for the 2026 race.

background.text: Ran as an independent candidate for Kentucky's 2nd District in 2018 against Guthrie and Democrat Hank Linderman; in a local newspaper questionnaire he named climate change as the most important issue facing the district.
